PROGRESS NOTE

History: The patient was evaluated two years ago for exertional dyspnea. At that time,
preoperative echocardiography of the native calcified valve showed a mean gradient of 52
mmHg with a calculated valve area consistent with severe stenosis. The patient subsequently
underwent surgical aortic valve replacement with a bioprosthesis.

Interval History: The patient now presents for a routine follow-up visit and reports no
chest pain, dyspnea, or syncope. Functional status remains stable at baseline.

Assessment: Status post aortic valve replacement, doing well. Today's transthoracic
echocardiogram was reviewed: the mean gradient is 13 mmHg across the well-functioning
prosthetic valve, essentially unchanged from prior surveillance studies. No significant
valvular regurgitation was noted.

Plan: Continue current medical therapy. Routine surveillance echocardiography in one year.
